title: runners.toml loader, validation, and substrate decision (internal/herd/config)
description: Go package internal/herd/config: parse .tick/runners.toml into typed structs mirroring skills/ticks/references/runners-config.schema.json (shape: additionalProperties-false equivalents, effort enum, model pattern rejecting colons); implement the documented semantics exactly — resolution order roles.R.tiers.T -> roles.R -> roles.implement with args replacing never merging; spawn-time compatibility fail-closed (kind vs model family per herdr-kinds.md: claude claude-family only, codex OpenAI only, pi provider-qualified cross-provider; unknown kind = error) with refusal messages naming role/tier + kind + model; model/effort -> native argv compilation per the herdr-kinds.md translation table (claude --model/--effort; codex -m + -c model_reasoning_effort=...; pi --model M:E). Implement the substrate decision procedure from runners-config.md: config-first (harness is terminal, no probe), then read-only probes (HERDR_ENV=1; socket ping via internal/herd/client), auto/herdr cells, explicit-degradation result type carrying requested substrate + failed probes + fallback for the caller to announce. This tick owns any new go.mod dependency (TOML parser — prefer an existing dependency already in go.mod if present, check first). Table-driven tests must include: every worked example from runners-config.md parsing + resolving identically to the doc, all schema-negative cases rejected, all four documented spawn-time refusals refusing, and the six substrate decision cells.
acceptance_criteria: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/herd/... passes; doc worked examples round-trip; six-cell decision table verified; refusal messages match the documented fail-closed rule
closed_reason: Completed: internal/herd/config — strict runners.toml loader (BurntSushi/toml for complete unknown-key reporting + present-vs-omitted), tier resolution with args-replace, per-kind compile with typed RefusalError fail-closed, six-cell substrate Decide with injectable prober; 93 cases incl. byte-for-byte doc argv round-trips
